question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 1)
options: Neither of the two proposals were accepted.
Each of the clerks has submitted his own form.
He is more taller than any other boy in his class.
The scenery of the hills are breathtaking.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb and pronoun.

question: Improve the part in capitals: She is one of those officers who ALWAYS COMPLETES her work on time.
explanation: 'Who' refers to the plural 'officers'.

question: Find the part with an error: Her performance (A) / in the interview was (B) / far better than any candidate. (C)
explanation: Illogical comparison: 'than any other candidate'.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The auditor's PERFUNCTORY inspection missed several irregularities.
explanation: Perfunctory means done with minimal effort.

question: The minister's statement was _____ by the media as an attempt to _____ public attention from the scam.
explanation: Critics brand it a diversion tactic.

question: The committee (A) / have decided to (B) / postpone it's meeting. (C)
explanation: 'its' (possessive) is correct; 'it's' means 'it is'.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The glory of the champion proved EPHEMERAL.
explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To have a chip on one's shoulder.
explanation: It means holding a lingering resentment.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The government has ANNOUNCED ABOUT a new housing scheme.
explanation: 'Announce' is transitive and takes no preposition.

question: Find the part with an error: Despite he was ill, (A) / he attended the (B) / meeting to present the report. (C)
explanation: 'Despite' cannot introduce a clause; use 'Although he was ill' or 'Despite his illness'.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The CEO tried to ALLEVIATE the concerns of investors.
explanation: Alleviate means to make less severe.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: She accepted the transfer with ALACRITY.
explanation: Alacrity is cheerful readiness.

question: Find the part with an error: A large number of applicants was (A) / present at the venue, but only (B) / a few of them had brought the required documents. (C)
explanation: 'A large number of' takes a plural verb, so 'was' should be 'were'.

question: Find the part with an error: Had the bank reviewed (A) / the loan more carefully, it would have (B) / avoided the subsequent default. (C)
explanation: A correct third conditional with inversion.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 8)
options: The reason he resigned is due because ill health.
The reason why he resigned is because of ill health.
Reason for him to resign was due because ill health.
He resigned because he was ill.
explanation: Only option B avoids redundancy and faulty constructions.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The auditor's findings CORROBORATED the whistle-blower's claims.
explanation: Corroborate means to support with evidence.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The minister described the scheme as a PANACEA for all the sector's ills.
explanation: A panacea is a remedy for all problems.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The teacher, along with her students, HAS GONE on an excursion.
explanation: The sentence is correct as it stands.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. A downgrade, in contrast, makes borrowing costlier.
Q. Credit rating agencies assess the ability of borrowers to repay their debts.
R. That is why governments and companies guard their ratings closely.
S. A high rating lets a borrower raise funds at a lower interest rate.
explanation: Definition, benefit, contrast, conclusion.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 20)
options: If I would have known, I would have told you.
Had I known, I will tell you.
Had I known, I would have told you.
If I had known, I would told you.
explanation: Inverted third conditional.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 18)
options: Each of the boys have a bicycle.
Each of the boys has a bicycle.
Each of the boys are having a bicycle.
Each of the boy has a bicycle.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb.

question: The bank's profits _____ sharply in the third quarter, _____ analysts' expectations.
explanation: Surge and exceeding expectations are consistent.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The former CEO has been ACCUSED WITH fraud and embezzlement.
explanation: The verb 'accuse' takes 'of'.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: He was a PROFLIGATE heir who squandered the family estate.
explanation: Profligate means wastefully extravagant.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To run out of steam.
explanation: It means exhausting one's drive.

question: Find the part with an error: She asked (A) / me whether did I (B) / know the answer. (C)
explanation: Reported question needs normal order: 'whether I knew'.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To cut corners.
options: To do something cheaply by skipping proper procedure
explanation: It implies neglecting thoroughness to save time or money.

question: Find the part with an error: The manager, who has (A) / been with the bank for two decades, (B) / is due to retire next year. (C)
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 10)
options: The principal along with the teachers were present.
Either of the two options are acceptable.
A number of students were absent today.
The number of students were large.
explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To steal a march on a rival.
options: To gain an advantage by acting first
To defeat a rival in a fair contest
explanation: It means getting ahead of someone secretly or early.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 14)
options: She told me that she would come.
She said me she would come.
She told that she would come.
She said to that she would come.
explanation: 'Tell' needs an indirect object.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The minister's EQUIVOCAL reply left reporters unsure of his stand.
explanation: Equivocal means open to more than one interpretation.

question: The prosecution's case was so strong, thanks to a _____ of evidence, that the court was compelled to _____ bail.
explanation: Abundant evidence leads to denial of bail.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To burn the midnight oil.
options: To work or study late into the night
To start a fire at night
explanation: It means working late at night.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The scandal TARNISHED the firm's reputation.
explanation: Tarnish means to damage or stain.

question: The government's _____ response to the crisis drew widespread _____ from the opposition.
explanation: A slow response draws criticism.

question: The author's later novels, though _____ in style, lack the _____ of his early work.
explanation: 'Though' needs contrast: polished but lacking vitality.

question: A leader who _____ credit for others' work soon loses the _____ of the team.
explanation: Taking credit wrongly destroys trust.

question: The scheme was launched with great _____ but soon _____ for want of funds.
explanation: Grand launch followed by failure.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The company's CIRCUMSPECT approach to expansion helped it survive the downturn.
explanation: Circumspect means wary of risks.
